text:
Arjun Mehta: Heads-up: I repro a dup write during large file uploads in sampleapp when the access token rotates and the server sends 429. Looks timing-sensitive but repeatable in staging.

Lena Ortiz: Which SDK/version and which endpoint?

Arjun Mehta: Node SDK v1.5.0 on sampleapp. Endpoint is /v1/uploads/append which does partial-chunk writes.

Priya Singh: Append semantics are tricky. If the client retries after refresh and server returned 429 to the in-flight chunk, we end up writing the chunk twice. Do we have any idempotency for chunked uploads?

Arjun Mehta: No, we don't. Current workaround is server-side dedupe based on content-hash, but that is expensive for large blobs and breaks for streaming where chunks vary. Logs: 

Arjun Mehta: ```
[2026-09-14T09:12:01Z] upload_id=u-123 chunk_seq=7 auth=expiring -> refresh start
[2026-09-14T09:12:01Z] refresh complete new_token=t-789
[2026-09-14T09:12:01Z] server responded 429 retry_after=2 for chunk_seq=7
[2026-09-14T09:12:03Z] sdk retry resend chunk_seq=7 without replay headers -> duplicate chunk written
```

Tom Becker: Two directions: (A) client-side per-chunk sequence + nonce header so server can dedupe by (upload_id, seq, nonce), or (B) make retries after auth refresh treated as "replays" by preserving original request context and sending an explicit Replay-Id header.

Priya Singh: Option A seems safer for streaming. We already assign chunk_seq for uploads. If we add `x-rw-chunk-nonce` that's per-upload unique and we enforce server dedupe for (upload_id, chunk_seq, nonce), duplicates are dropped.

Lena Ortiz: We also need to avoid adding heavy sync ops on the server hot path. Proposed server contract: store short-lived dedupe keys in in-RAM sharded map for 90s, async persist hits to opaque metadata store. Return 409 with body {"replayed": true, "seq": n} on duplicate. Is 90s okay?

Tom Becker: 90s fine. Also client should expose `retryStrategy` config: default to truncated-exp-backoff with jitter in [0.6,1.4] multiplier and max backoff 10s. Current jitter range causes clustered retries. Make jitter tunable per-client.

Arjun Mehta: I can prototype `x-rw-chunk-nonce` plus sending `x-rw-client-replay-id` when refresh happens. Also add quick opt-in client flag `enable_safe_replay: true` which sets those headers and keeps tiny LRU of recent request hashes for 2 min.

Priya Singh: Good to keep opt-in to avoid perf surprises. Add telemetry events: replay_attempt, replay_dedup_hit, replay_dedup_miss, replay_latency_ms.

Lena Ortiz: Important UX note: update onboarding docs and sampleapp README with guidance: "avoid token TTL < 30s for large uploads; enable enable_safe_replay for long-lived requests".

Tom Becker: One more idea: when refresh occurs, SDK can attempt to cancel inflight request (if underlying transport allows) and then re-issue with replay headers. That reduces ambiguous server-side 429s. But cancel semantics vary by platform. Worth trying in Node.

Arjun Mehta: I'll add a small e2e that forces TTL=3s on staging to hit the case and run with safe_replay enabled. Will open PR with prototype + tests for streaming chunk dupes.

ci-bot: sampleapp/pr-521 started CI. Unit tests running. :running: 

Priya Singh: Please include a perf bench showing LRU hit overhead < 0.3ms per request. If it's more, we need to revisit default off.

Lena Ortiz: I'll coordinate with eng-runtime to review the server dedupe implementation. pinging them after this thread.

Arjun Mehta: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link and a tiny repro script once CI finishes.
